_comment: Example configuration for Toolbelt's git config generator. Copy this file, then replace values to match your own preferences. This repo intentionally ships an example (not my personal config).

patterns: Patterns are matched against configured Git remote URLs (the script uses remote.*.url, so it can match any remote name, not just 'origin').
Use the same format you see in: git remote get-url origin (SSH, SSH Host Alias or HTTPS).
Each pattern is the base URL up to (and including) the user/org. The script appends /** automatically for repos.
The user/org segment can be a specific name (e.g. 'your-user') to match only that account, or * to match any user/org on that host or SSH alias.
To disable conditional identities entirely, set 'identities' to an empty array: []
usage: This repo ships an example gitconfig.json. Copy it and customize it for your own environment.
After editing this file, re-run the script to (re)generate the identity files (e.g., ~/.gitconfig_work) and update your global git config (~/.gitconfig).
If you use multiple remotes (origin/upstream/fork), remember the tool can match any of them (remote.*.url). If a repo has both a work and personal remote configured, multiple identities may match.
largeRepos: If you run the script with -RepoPath, it ONLY applies largeRepoSettings to that repo and skips global settings/aliases/identities.
largeRepoSettings are optional. Some settings (like core.fsmonitor) may require additional setup depending on OS/Git version.
security: Don't commit private tokens/credentials in this file, especially if it's in a public repo.
Emails/names are usually fine to commit if you intend them to be public.
